description:
FOUND s509 (Fable, 2026-10-06), the speed review.  docs/speed-review-s509.md; measurements and profiles in ~/pcl-agent-scratch/s509/review/speed/ (prof.pl ROW... -> ROW.pl, ROW.lisp, ROW.prof; main b43188b5, gen v2-4280, load 5-6, best of 3-5)

PROFILE (grepcnt.prof; `my $k = grep $_, @p` over 20 elements, 200 k times; perl 0.083 s, main 0.177 s):
  `p-grep` 86 % total (22 % self); `%p-collect-list` 26 % total; `vector-hairy-data-vector-ref/check-bounds` +
  `slow-hairy-data-vector-ref/check-bounds` 15 %; `%p-true-p-slow` + `%pcl-nan-p` 14 %; `prepare-vector-push-extend` 4 %.
THREE SMALL CHANGES inside `p-grep` (and its expression-form twin, if it is a second copy -- look first, rule 11):
  1. scalar / boolean context: COUNT, do not collect (the context is already known where *wantarray* is read);
  2. read the source through its data vector (`%p-vec-data`, as the foreach arms do) instead of `aref` on the adjustable array;
  3. the truthiness test takes the fixnum fast path before the general one.
EXPECTED: -35 to -45 % on grepcnt.  `if (grep { ... } @list)`, `my $n = grep ...`, `scalar(grep ...)` are ordinary code.
BREAKING CASES to probe vs perl: a grep block that modifies `$_` (aliasing must survive change 2), a tied array, `grep`
over a list that is not an array, a block that calls `last` / dies, nested grep, `wantarray` inside the block.
subject: PERF, MEASURED s509 (lever C): `grep` in SCALAR context builds the list it only counts -- `my $k = grep $_, @p`: `%p-collect-list` 26 %, adjustable-vector element reads 15 %, slow truthiness on small integers 14 % (grepcnt 2.1x perl)
